readings.reading: The output is a fixed 3x3 pattern of 8 chosen by the input's most common non-background colour: 1 -> [008,880,080], 3 -> [088,080,080], 2 -> [000,888,000].
readings.why: the output depends only on the majority colour; equal majority colours give identical outputs

readings.reading: The 7x7 input is noise dominated by one colour (1, 2 or 3); the output is a fixed 3x3 colour-8 pattern chosen by that dominant colour (1 -> 008/880/080, 2 -> 000/888/000, 3 -> 088/080/080).
readings.why: pairs with the same dominant colour have identical outputs; output is always 3x3

readings.reading: The 7x7 input is noise dominated by one colour (1, 2 or 3). The output is a fixed 3x3 glyph of colour 8 chosen by that dominant colour: 1 -> [008,880,080], 2 -> [000,888,000], 3 -> [088,080,080].
readings.why: every pair's output equals the glyph for its input's majority non-zero colour

readings.reading: The input is noise dominated by one colour (1, 2 or 3). The output is a fixed 3x3 pattern in colour 8 chosen by that dominant colour: 1 -> 008/880/080, 2 -> 000/888/000, 3 -> 088/080/080.
readings.why: every pair's output is the pattern listed for its majority colour

readings.reading: The output is a fixed 3x3 pattern of 8s chosen by the dominant non-background colour of the input: 1 -> 008/880/080, 2 -> 000/888/000, 3 -> 088/080/080.
readings.why: on every pair the output equals the table entry for the input's most common non-zero colour

readings.reading: Each isolated single cell gets a 3x3 ring around it whose colour depends on the cell colour: 3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1; the centre cell stays.
readings.why: every marker's 8 neighbours become key(marker colour); nothing else changes

readings.reading: Each isolated marker cell is surrounded by a 3x3 ring; the ring colour depends on the marker colour (3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1). The marker itself stays.
readings.why: every marker's 8 neighbours take the mapped colour; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Every isolated single cell gets a 3x3 square ring around it, and the ring colour depends on the centre colour (3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1).
readings.why: each marker's 8 neighbours take the mapped colour; the marker cell itself stays; all other cells unchanged

readings.reading: Each isolated marker cell gets a 3x3 ring around it (marker kept in the centre). The ring colour depends on the marker colour: 3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1.
readings.why: every marker's 8 neighbours become key(marker colour); all other cells unchanged

readings.reading: Each isolated coloured cell gets a 3x3 ring around it, ring colour set by the cell's colour (3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1); the centre stays.
readings.why: every marker is the centre of a 3x3 square ring whose colour is a fixed function of the marker colour; all other cells unchanged

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a grid of (number of background cells) x (number of background cells) blocks; the first k blocks in reading order (k = number of foreground cells) hold a copy of the input, the rest are empty.
readings.why: each output block is the input or empty; copies = fg pixel count, filled row-major; blocks per side = bg pixel count

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is copied N times (N = number of non-background cells) into an output of B x B blocks (B = number of background cells), filling blocks in reading order; remaining blocks stay empty.
readings.why: every 3x3 block is the input or empty; count of copies = fg cell count, blocks per side = bg cell count

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into an N x N block grid where N is the number of background cells; the first K blocks in reading order get a copy of the input, K being the number of foreground cells; the rest stay empty.
readings.why: every 3x3 block of the output is either the input or all background; copies count = fg pixel count, filled row-major; output side = 3 x bg count

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is copied into an n x n grid of 3x3 blocks, where n is the number of background cells; the number of copies equals the number of non-background cells, laid out in reading order from the top-left, the rest of the blocks empty.
readings.why: each output block is the input or empty; #copies = #fg cells, blocks per side = #bg cells, copies fill row-major

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a square of (number of background cells) x (number of background cells) blocks; the first k blocks in row-major order hold a copy, where k is the number of coloured cells, the rest are empty.
readings.why: output side = 3 * (#bg cells); blocks 1..#fg (row-major) equal the input, all other blocks are 0

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is scaled up by 3: every cell becomes a 3x3 block of its colour.
readings.why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3)

readings.reading: Each input cell is scaled up into a 3x3 block of its colour (3x upscale).
readings.why: output size is 3x input size and each 3x3 block is uniform with the colour of the corresponding input cell

readings.reading: Each input cell is enlarged to a 3x3 block of its colour (scale by 3).
readings.why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3) on every pair

readings.reading: Every input cell is scaled up into a 3x3 block of its colour (3x3 -> 9x9).
readings.why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3)

readings.reading: Every input cell is enlarged to a 3x3 block of its colour (scale up by 3).
readings.why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3)

readings.reading: Four isolated 5-cells mark the sides of a box; a rectangle outline in the colour of the central shape is drawn one cell inside the markers (rows/cols just inside the topmost, bottommost, leftmost and rightmost markers).
readings.why: the outline passes exactly one cell inside each of the four markers; everything else unchanged

readings.reading: Four grey(5) marker cells lie above, below, left and right of a hollow shape; a rectangle outline in the shape's colour is drawn one cell inside the markers' bounding box.
readings.why: the new outline is exactly the perimeter of the inset marker box; markers and the shape stay unchanged

readings.reading: Four colour-5 marker cells (top, bottom, left, right) bound a box; a rectangle outline in the colour of the hollow shape is drawn one cell inside the markers.
readings.why: the outline cells lie exactly one step inside each marker; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Four colour-5 markers (top, bottom, left, right) bound a box; a rectangle outline in the colour of the small hollow shape is drawn one cell inside the markers, i.e. on rows top+1 and bottom-1 and columns left+1 and right-1.
readings.why: the only changed cells are the outline of the rectangle [top+1..bottom-1] x [left+1..right-1], painted in the shape's colour

readings.reading: Four single marker cells (colour 5) bound a rectangle; draw its outline one cell inside the markers, in the colour of the other shape, keeping everything else.
readings.why: the added cells are exactly the outline of the rectangle inset by one from the four markers, coloured like the shape

readings.reading: Full separator lines cut the grid into equal cells; one cell holds a pattern, which is copied into every cell whose row index and column index have the same parity as that cell's (every second cell in both directions).
readings.why: every same-parity cell equals the source cell; other cells and separators unchanged

readings.reading: Separator lines cut the grid into equal cells; one cell holds a pattern. The pattern is copied into every cell whose row index and column index differ from the source cell's by an even number (every second cell in both directions).
readings.why: every panel with same parity as the source equals the source; all other panels stay empty; separators unchanged

readings.reading: A lattice of separator lines splits the grid into equal cells; one cell holds a pattern. The pattern is copied into every cell whose cell-row and cell-column differ from the source cell's by an even number.
readings.why: every cell with the source's cell-index parity in both directions equals the source pattern; others remain empty

readings.reading: The grid is divided into equal cells by full separator lines; one cell holds a small pattern. The pattern is copied into every cell whose row index and column index differ from the pattern cell's by an even number (every second cell in both directions).
readings.why: a panel cell holds the pattern iff its (row, col) cell index has the same parity as the source cell; all other cells stay empty

readings.reading: The grid is cut into equal cells by separator lines; one cell holds a pattern, which is copied into every cell whose row and column indices have the same parity as the source cell (every second cell in both directions).
readings.why: every compartment with the source's parity in both directions equals the source; others stay empty

readings.reading: The top row (above a full 5 separator) lists colours c0,c1,c2,...; around the single marker below, concentric square rings are drawn: ring k (Chebyshev distance k) gets colour ck, clipped at the grid edge.
readings.why: every cell within distance len(palette)-1 of the marker has palette[distance]; area outside unchanged

readings.reading: The top row is a colour legend; around the single marker below the separator, concentric square rings are drawn, ring at Chebyshev distance r taking legend colour r (r=0 is the centre), clipped at the grid edge.
readings.why: every cell within the legend length of the marker has the legend colour of its ring distance; legend and separator unchanged (pair 0 output also shows legend cell 5 turned from 8 to 5, unexplained)

readings.reading: A key row above a separator lists colours k0,k1,k2,...; around the single marker below, concentric square rings are drawn: the centre keeps k0 and the ring at Chebyshev distance d gets colour k_d (colour 0 rings stay background).
readings.why: every cell below the separator at distance d < len(key) has colour key[d]

readings.reading: The top row (above a separator line of 5) is a colour key c0,c1,c2,...; around the single marker below, concentric square rings are drawn: the centre keeps c0, ring k (Chebyshev distance k) gets colour ck, for as many key entries as given (0 entries leave a background ring).
readings.why: every cell within distance len(key)-1 of the marker has colour key[distance]; cells farther away unchanged

readings.reading: The top row is a colour key k0,k1,k2,...; the single cell of colour k0 below the separator becomes the centre of concentric square rings, ring at distance d coloured k_d.
readings.why: every cell at Chebyshev distance d from the marker has colour key[d] for d < key length

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each diagonal corner of it a 2x2 block (clipped by the grid) is painted in the colour of the diagonally opposite cell of the block.
readings.why: each corner area is uniformly the opposite block colour; block unchanged

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each of its four diagonal corners a 2x2 block is placed (clipped at edges) coloured with the colour of the diagonally opposite cell of the block.
readings.why: each outside 2x2 corner block is uniform with the opposite block colour; the original block unchanged

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each of its four diagonal corners a 2x2 block is drawn in the colour of the diagonally opposite cell of the block (clipped at the border).
readings.why: top-left target = bottom-right colour, top-right = bottom-left, bottom-left = top-right, bottom-right = top-left

readings.reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each of its four diagonal corners a 2x2 block is painted (clipped to the grid) in the colour of the block cell diagonally opposite that corner.
readings.why: each corner 2x2 area is filled with the colour of the diagonally opposite block cell; the block itself unchanged

readings.reading: A 2x2 block [a b / c d] gets four 2x2 blocks added diagonally off its corners, each coloured with the diagonally opposite cell: d at top-left, c at top-right, b at bottom-left, a at bottom-right (clipped at the border).
readings.why: each corner 2x2 region is filled with the opposite corner's colour; the original block is unchanged

readings.reading: Four L-shaped corner brackets mark a rectangle; the 1-pattern inside each rectangle is completed by mirroring it about the rectangle's centre line (left-right or up-down, whichever makes it symmetric), and stray 1-cells outside every rectangle are erased.
readings.why: inside each frame the 1-pattern is symmetric about the frame's centre line; no 1 lies outside a frame

readings.reading: Frames are marked by four L-shaped corner brackets; the colour-1 pattern inside each frame is completed by mirroring it across the frame's midline along its long side (union with its reflection), and stray colour-1 cells outside all frames are erased.
readings.why: inside each frame the 1-pattern is symmetric about the frame's midline and contains the input pattern; no 1 cells remain outside frames

readings.reading: Each box marked by four corner brackets contains some 1-cells in one half; that half is mirrored across the box's centre line (along its long side) so the content is symmetric, and all stray 1-cells outside the boxes are erased.
readings.why: inside every box the content is mirror-symmetric about its centre line; no colour-1 cell remains outside boxes

readings.reading: Rectangular frames are marked by four L-shaped corner brackets; the colour-1 pattern inside each frame occupies one half and is mirrored across the frame's centre line (perpendicular to its long side) so the interior becomes symmetric. Stray colour-1 cells outside any frame are erased.
readings.why: inside every frame the 1-pattern is symmetric about the frame's midline and contains the original; no 1-cells remain outside frames

readings.reading: Four L-shaped corner brackets mark each box; the 1-pattern inside each box is completed to be symmetric about the box centre (mirror left-right or top-bottom, whichever half is empty), and stray 1s outside all boxes are erased.
readings.why: inside every box the 1-pattern is symmetric about the box centre line; no 1 lies outside a box

readings.reading: Full 5 lines cut the grid into blocks; the top-left block is filled with 1, the centre block (middle row band and middle column band) with 2, and the bottom-right block with 3.
readings.why: exactly those three blocks are filled; separators and other blocks unchanged

readings.reading: Full grey separator lines cut the grid into cells; the top-left cell is filled with 1, the centre cell (middle row band, middle column band) with 2, and the bottom-right cell with 3.
readings.why: exactly those three panels are filled solid with their colours; separators and other panels unchanged

readings.reading: Full lines of colour 5 cut the grid into cells; the top-left cell is filled with 1, the middle cell (middle cell-row and middle cell-column) with 2, and the bottom-right cell with 3.
readings.why: exactly those three lattice cells become solid colour 1, 2, 3; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Full lines of 5 cut the grid into panels; the top-left panel is filled with 1, the centre panel (middle row band, middle column band) with 2, and the bottom-right panel with 3.
readings.why: only those three panels change, each filled entirely with its constant colour

readings.reading: Full separator lines cut the grid into compartments; the top-left compartment is filled with 1, the centre compartment with 2, and the bottom-right compartment with 3.
readings.why: exactly those three compartments are filled with 1, 2, 3; everything else unchanged
